title: Workload-phased burst contracts and latency funds — PRD outline
content:
Context / motivation:
We keep getting two related asks from larger customers and platform leads: (1) predictable tail latency guarantees during demand surges, and (2) an economically clear way to buy temporary capacity beyond a reserved pool without blowing committed cost targets. Current 'burst credit' sketches are noisy: too binary (you either have credits or you don't), and they don't align with SLAs that are latency-budgeted per-route.

Idea summary (high level):
Introduce a workload-phased burst contract model combined with a user-visible 'latency fund'. Customers can commit to a baseline Dedicated reservation (same as today) and then purchase one or more phased burst contracts that provide time-boxed additional headroom with explicit latency budget consumption semantics. The platform exposes a latency fund meter per-tenant (and per-route optionally) that gets debited when the system uses burst capacity to keep requests within latency SLOs.

Why this is different / benefits:
- Finer-grained economics: customers pay for burst capacity that’s explicitly tied to latency protection, not opaque credits.
- Predictable behavior: contracts specify phase windows (e.g., daily peak 08:00–10:00, weekend batch) and pricing tiers per phase.
- Better isolation: burst allocations are scoped by route/priority so noisy tenants can be gated without evicting baseline capacity.
- Operational clarity: SRE and CS can reason about fund depletion, auto-topups, and emergency throttles.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Implement a prototype allocation and tracking system that can be toggled per-tenant by Q2 2025.
- Reduce unplanned evictions by 40% in trials (compared to current best-effort bursts).
- Offer 3 pricing/phase templates (seasonal, daily-peak, ad-hoc) for pilot customers.
- Expose latency fund telemetry in Console and alert when fund hits configurable thresholds.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not define final pricing; we'll iterate with finance.
- Not covering on-prem private deployments in the first wave — hosted and dedicated only.

Concept details / mechanics:
1) Phased Burst Contracts
   - Definition: a contract is (tenant, phase_id, window, capacity_quota, latency_priority, price). Example: tenant AcmeCorp phase: morning-peak, window 08:00–10:00 PST, extra 200 qps, priority low/medium/high, price $X/hr.
   - Phases can be recurring (daily) or ad-hoc (single-day). Phases can overlap; resolution rules defined below.

2) Latency Fund
   - Each tenant has a numeric fund balance (units = latency-seconds or normalized credit).
   - When the platform routes requests to burst capacity to keep them under the tenant’s SLO, the fund is debited proportionally to the time-on-burst and requested token volume.
   - Fund controls: auto-topup (monthly cap), manual recharge, emergency escrow held by ops.

3) Allocation & Routing policy
   - Requests are tagged with route priority and SLO. The broker decides if a request can be placed on baseline, queued (short wait), or routed to burst.
   - If burst used: decrement fund, mark trace and cost. If fund = 0 -> degrade to best-effort fallback (longer queue or lower-fidelity model).

4) Isolation controls and fairness
   - Soft isolation: phase allocations are soft guarantees (best-effort but prioritized over opportunistic pool).
   - Hard isolation mode (optional): a tenant can buy a hard cap for a phase (reserved GPUs for the window) — higher price, stronger eviction protection.
   - Cross-tenant fairness: a priority comparator that considers (phase priority, remaining fund, baseline SLO headroom).

APIs / user flows:
- Console: phase management UI (create phase, set window/quantity/priority, view fund balance). Alerts to set thresholds e.g., 30% remaining.
- REST API: POST /tenants/{id}/phases, GET /tenants/{id}/latency-fund, POST /tenants/{id}/funds/recharge
- Billing: phase purchases tied to billing cycle; over-usage beyond purchased quota billed as on-demand at a higher rate.

Telemetry & observability:
- Metrics: fund_balance, fund_debits_total, bursts_allocated, burst_steals (requests sent to burst when baseline busy), tail_p99_by_phase, evictions_due_to_fund_depletion.
- Traces: tag requests that touch burst; attach phase_id for drill-down.
- Console: per-tenant heatmap of fund usage by route and time-of-day.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Normal ops: CS monitors fund burn; set auto-topups for customers that prefer that.
- When fund depletion rate > X% over 5m: notify CS and SRE, trigger advisory throttling on lowest priority routes.
- Emergency: ops can inject temporary fund credit or enable a limited hard-isolation slice for 30m.

Data model sketch (informal):
- tenant_id: string
- phases: list of {phase_id, window_cron-ish, capacity_qps, priority, mode(hard/soft), price_ref}
- fund_balance: number (float)
- fund_policy: {auto_topup_threshold, topup_amount, max_monthly_charge}

Pricing & commerce notes (open):
- We need pricing prototypes: fixed hourly for hard-isolation slices, capacity-bracket pricing for soft burst, and per-latency-second rate for overage. Finance involvement required.

Migration / backward compatibility:
- Default: tenants with existing burst-credit features map to 'soft' phase auto-generated covering 00:00–23:59 with legacy conversion ratio.
- Beta customers can opt-in; no change to tenants that do nothing.

Rollout plan (stages):
- Stage 0 (internal): prototype in staging (allocator + fund accounting) — 4 weeks.
- Stage 1 (beta): enable for 3 pilot customers, hosted + dedicated pilot pools — 8 weeks.
- Stage 2 (GA): Console + billing + docs + 90-day ramp — Q3 2025.

Risks & mitigations:
- Accounting correctness: fund reconciliation mismatch -> build end-of-day ledger and independent verifier job.
- Complexity for customers: provide templates and recommended presets; CS-led onboarding.
- Attack surface: tenants could game priorities — restrict per-route allocs and require owner signoff for priority escalation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to quantify fund debits precisely (tokens vs time on GPU vs queue time)? TODO: prototype models and bench on sample workloads.
- What are sensible default phase windows and pricing tiers? Finance + GTM workshop.
- Integration with Dedicated autoscaler: can spectral autoscaler pre-warm GPU islands for upcoming high-priority phases? Action: sync with infra-autoscale team (Ravi).

Notes from related threads:
- Slack: #dedicated-capacity -> thread titled "latency funds" has early CS asks (tagging Aisha).
- GitHub: initial allocator changes PR referenced above; needs more telemetry hooks.

Immediate next steps:
1) Do a short feasibility spike: implement fund accounting skeleton + simple broker hook (2 engineers x 1 week).
2) Run a tabletop scenario with SRE/CS to validate runbook and emergency flow.
3) Draft pricing options for pilot and schedule finance sync.

Comments welcome — this is intentionally rough. Looking for prioritization feedback and whether to fold this into the existing burst-credit workstream or spin it into a separate pilot track.

-- Evan
